chief_complaint: Management of hypertension and associated cardiometabolic risk factors
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 39-year-old woman with a history of essential hypertension diagnosed in 2019, currently on low‑dose hydrochlorothiazide. Blood pressure recorded at the most recent visit (128/90 mmHg) meets criteria for stage 2 hypertension, indicating suboptimal control. Obesity (BMI ≥30) was documented in 2023, and prediabetes has been present since 2016 with an A1c of 6.2%. Anemia was first noted in 2020 and she receives monthly vitamin B12 injections, suggesting a possible B12‑deficiency macrocytic anemia. Chronic sinusitis has been longstanding. Over the past year she has experienced social isolation, unstable housing, and a transition to full‑time employment, all of which may impact adherence and lifestyle. No acute complaints are recorded; recent encounters have been primarily wellness visits.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple episodes of gingivitis and a tooth infection (most recent resolution 2023-05-13), prior periods of unemployment (resolved 2023-04-29), past reports of environmental violence (resolved 2022-04-23), previous stress episodes (resolved 2023-04-29), and earlier medication review prompts (resolved 2022-04-22). These reflect a background of dental disease and fluctuating social circumstances.

risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: stage 2 hypertension (SBP 128, DBP 90), obesity, prediabetes (A1c 6.2%). Hematologic risk: anemia treated with B12, suggesting possible macrocytic anemia. Metabolic risk: likely metabolic syndrome; lipid panel and renal function (eGFR) are missing, limiting full risk assessment. ENT risk: chronic sinusitis. Psychosocial risk: housing instability, social isolation, and risk‑activity involvement. Charlson comorbidity index is 1, clinical complexity moderate.

clinical_impression: The patient presents with a high‑risk cardiometabolic profile—stage 2 hypertension, obesity, and prediabetes—compounded by anemia likely due to B12 deficiency and chronic sinusitis. Social determinants such as unstable housing and isolation further jeopardize disease control. Current therapy appears insufficient for blood pressure and metabolic risk, and key laboratory data (lipids, renal function, detailed anemia studies) are missing, limiting comprehensive risk stratification.
